answer: Each identity must publish a chained verifiable-delay-function transcript per epoch: one hash chain that cannot be parallelized, so a single machine's wall-clock time is a hollow shell compared to the identities it claims. Attempts to split computation across GPUs add only velvet-smooth overhead, never shortcut the mandated delay. Sybil scale becomes linear in calendar time, the one resource an attacker cannot fake in bulk.
